second_order: passing around and reacting to the eggs joke
theme_note: These passages hold together because people recruit others into saving the eggs, rhyme with the call, or reject the same Easter meme; what varies is joining the bit versus complaining about it.
People divide a named r/place inscription into letters and report its completion; contributions vary by letter, with a separate neighbor-avoidance turn grouped under negotiation instead.

second_order: asking what Place is and whether anyone is on board
theme_note: This single exchange opens a deleted Place thread, asks what it means, and doubts turnout; it belongs with no other practice strongly enough to merge.

second_order: pulling and answering April Fools jokes
theme_note: Across separate non-canvas exchanges, people announce fake news, misidentify Donald, prank one another, congratulate, curse, or complain; the shared practice is doing and answering the subreddit’s own April Fools jokes, while targets and reactions vary.

second_order: calling people into new canvas builds
theme_note: These passages propose named pictures, ask for hands, seek outside help, or organize another attempt; what varies is the target and whether the call comes before, during, or after a completed picture.

second_order: building and updating BTI across locations
theme_note: People place pixels, work borders around other obligations, check whether work remains, and report coordinates or progress; locations and stages vary, but the practice is keeping a distributed build actionable on Reddit.

People name flags, erasers, logos, rival targets, and later the Void as things to destroy, take over, spare, mock, or resist; what varies is whether the language addresses impersonal overwriting, a proposed attack, or an accusation from another group.

second_order: moving the BTI build after it keeps failing
theme_note: These passages abandon erased or blocked sites, announce new ones, and recount repeated BTI failure; the trigger varies by site, while the repeated practice is relocating rather than holding one position.

second_order: backing off occupied art and parting on good terms
theme_note: Visible encounters with neighbors lead builders to avoid, move, apologize, accept an apology, offer help, or thank one another; the neighboring pictures vary, and these negotiated exchanges are kept apart from generic attack talk.

second_order: putting place talk into the megathread
theme_note: The moderator centralizes scattered updates and later removes or redirects posts under that rule; what varies is creating the rule versus enforcing it.

second_order: moving live organizing from Reddit to Discord
theme_note: People share Discord with templates and positions, direct confused builders there, join it, and carry requests between venues; what varies is invitation, referral, joining, and returning an update.

second_order: celebrating the finished Kauai picture together
theme_note: Participants report completion, celebrate, claim or repost the achievement, thank a repairer, and later thank everyone; what varies is claiming a contribution, repeating the announcement, or offering collective thanks.

second_order: crediting other subreddits for help and room
theme_note: These passages thank or describe r/Kanye, r/frankocean, and their members as helping, sharing space, or overlapping with the project; the claimed relationship varies, but each allocates credit beyond this subreddit.

second_order: repairing and changing the finished picture
theme_note: After completion, people maintain pixels, fix damage, petition for an alteration, and later defend Kauai from the Void; what varies is routine repair, proposed improvement, and emergency defense.

second_order: saying goodbye to place after it ends
theme_note: The early slice contributes a late mourning turn; later codes can extend this practice where people announce closure, mourn, thank participants, or interpret the finished event.

second_order: turning the finished canvas into posters to remember it
theme_note: People offer, order, preserve details in, and set reminders for r/place posters as ways to remember participation and shared work; poster type and buyer response vary.
A seller and critics dispute whether charging for the shared canvas is robbery or ordinary production and shipping; accusation, mockery, and justification are contrasting turns in the same practice.
